items.d: Opened in 1896 and rebuilt in 2006 after an earthquake, this has a capacity of 20,000. It hosts the combined Windies Test team, the Trinidad & Tobago island team, and Trinbago Knight Riders in the T20 Caribbean Premier League.
Built in 1659. Functions as the administrative headquarters of Trashigang district. Houses the local branch of the monastic body.
Breath taking views and friendly shop keepers.

Daily, Brazilian National Congress offers a guided visit. It starts every half hour from 09:00, in Salão Negro (access the main ramp). It lasts for 50 minutes. You cannot enter wearing shorts and slippers from Monday to Friday.
This is the smaller temple to the right.
The largest oceanarium in Russia, and one of the largest ones in Europe. Standard, but impressive variety of marine species is complemented with a wide array of Russia's freshwater species of fish.

An area with interesting shops and most importantly, a series of residential buildings called "les Schtroumpfs" (1982-1984), where the architects tried to avoid all straight lines, leading to an unconventional Gaudi-like…
The Jami Masjid, or the Main Mosque, lies just south of the Hawa Mahal. It is a gigantic mosque and approached by a long flight of stairs.
Beautiful house of worship built by the French in 1910, renovated in 2004.
In the first floor, the museum houses displays of silver jewellery for women and horses, and replicas of the golden bull- and wolf-head sculptures from Altyn Depe.
If you're walking between old town and the upper train station, don't miss the fantastic murals while taking the underpass below the big bridge roundabout crossing the Teplá.
A dam was built in the 1970s for hydroelectricity production, and the artificial lake is surrounded by beautiful mountains. Trout is cultivated in many places around the lake.

The hike takes about 1 hr, and on a mist-less day (e.g. during wet season when the air is cleaned by the rain) you can easily spot Bagan. About 1 km before the peak, you will hit a small temple with pagoda.
Quneitra is a ghost town, which was abandoned by the Syrians during the 1967 war and left in the no-man's-land ever since.
The tomb of Khan Jahan Ali is a major pilgrimage site in the area, and hundreds of visitors stop here daily to pay their respects to one of the country's more famous holy men.
Original area of the town.

An NGO project to bring city gardening and nature to the city centre. You can walk there for free, have a picnic or join some of their periodic activities.
The remains of a royal fortified city that was founded by Fasilides (Fasil), emperor of Ethiopia from 1632 to 1667, and was the home of the emperors in the 17th and 18th centuries.
Remains of a 1790 fort built to protect the harbour.
A beautiful black cliff and coastal area, which is great for sunsets. The rock formation is supposed to look like a lying cat, with a lot of imagination.

It has 640 crosses. They mark the graves of the French soldiers that died there in the conflicts of the First World War.
Dates from the 6th century and covers an area of about 20 ha. It consists of a wall and moat. The surviving walls are up to 30 m high.

Unusual museum owned by the Lo Heng Mong motorbike shop. In business for more than 50 years, the business has kept an example of most motorcycles they have sold over that period. Most motorcycles are small-displacement scooters.
By the Bonny Jetty where seafood is sold.
One-way and return cable car ticket available. Wheelchair accessible throughout, with a separate lift entrance and friendly staff will help accessibility visitors.

items.d: Start here for orientation and background on the ruins. There's an interesting exhibition and an audio-visual show. Guided tours of the Monastic City are available in multiple languages all year round by advance booking.
If you were to be executed during the khan's rule, it was probably going to happen in the center of this once-busy square.

items.d: This is the main produce market in town, but also sells some local crafts. Local fruits and vegetables, some of the best and freshest in the world, are sold here.
The well supposedly used by Abraham.

The spa and sauna center features a swimming pool, cold water pool and Japanese pool, small children’s pool, jacuzzi and foot baths, 2 steam baths, juniper sauna, Finnish sauna, birch sauna, aroma sauna, salt room, Garra Rufa…

A 100-m waterfall rushing down a granite cliff into a pool deep in the forest. The waterfall is at the end of a 40-minute hike along narrow paths that wind through hillside cocoa plantations before entering the forest.

A sandy beach with a lifeguard located by a quiet, charming lake. Good escape from usual noise of such lakes. Beware as it gets deep relatively fast, no car access, park your car by Greiser road (about 1 km walk).
Private shore diving for 2 to 4 divers with an SSI and PADI instructor: discovery dives from age 10, guided dives for certified divers and courses.
That Byin Nyu Temple was built in the mid-12th century during the reign of King Alaungsithu. Adjacent to Ananda Temple, it is the tallest structure in Bagan.

By the time it is completed, it will be a residential, commercial and educational haven. Reem Island is progressing well, with many skyscrapers being built on the island to facilitate its growing population.
Romanesque church dating from the 12th century. It is obligatory to reserve by phone.
